work_item.title: Dark/Light Theme Implementation
work_item.description: 🚩 AC Addressed (Required) Introduce light/dark theme selection entirely within the existing Python-rendered web UI. Ensure query syntax highlighting and result panels remain legible under both themes. Persist the user’s theme choice across requests using local storage. 💡 What do you want to accomplish? (Required) Improve user experience by allow users to toggle between dark/light themes. 📋 Testability Considerations (Required) Unit tests to check the new dark/light theme functionality.
acceptance_criteria: Users can toggle between dark and light themes via the UI.
Query syntax highlighting colors adapt appropriately to the selected theme and remain legible.
Result panels display content clearly under both themes.
User's theme preference is saved in local storage and applied automatically on subsequent page loads.
Unit tests cover theme toggling logic and persistence.

analysis.summary: Implement a dark/light theme toggle within the existing Python-rendered web UI, ensuring syntax highlighting and result panels remain legible, with user preference persisted via local storage.
technical_requirements: Add light/dark theme selection functionality integrated into the existing Python-rendered web UI.
Ensure query syntax highlighting and result panels are visually legible under both themes.
Persist the user's theme choice across requests using local storage.
Implement unit tests to verify dark/light theme functionality.
acceptance_criteria: Users can toggle between dark and light themes via the UI.
Query syntax highlighting colors adapt appropriately to the selected theme and remain legible.
Result panels display content clearly under both themes.
User's theme preference is saved in local storage and applied automatically on subsequent page loads.
Unit tests cover theme toggling logic and persistence.
risks: Ensuring consistent and accessible color contrast for syntax highlighting and UI elements across themes.
Integrating theme toggling smoothly within the existing Python-rendered UI without disrupting current functionality.
Cross-browser compatibility of local storage usage and CSS changes.
Potential increase in maintenance complexity due to theme-specific styles.
analysis.recommended_approach: Implement CSS variables or separate CSS classes for dark and light themes and toggle them via JavaScript. Modify the Python-rendered templates to include theme-related classes or attributes. Use local storage to save and retrieve the user's theme preference on page load. Update syntax highlighting logic or styles to support both themes. Develop unit tests focusing on theme toggle functionality and persistence.

implementation_steps.description: Add CSS variables for light and dark themes in styles.py and update existing styles to use these variables for background, text, primary colors, and syntax highlighting.

instructions: Define CSS variables for light theme: --bg-color: #f8f9fa, --text-color: #333333, --primary-color: #0066cc, --syntax-keyword: #00008b, --syntax-string: #a31515, --syntax-comment: #008000, --panel-bg: #ffffff, --panel-text: #000000.

Define CSS variables for dark theme inside a .dark-theme class: --bg-color: #1a1a1a, --text-color: #e0e0e0, --primary-color: #4da6ff, --syntax-keyword: #569cd6, --syntax-string: #d69d85, --syntax-comment: #6a9955, --panel-bg: #2d2d2d, --panel-text: #e0e0e0.
Refactor existing body, panel, and syntax highlighting styles to use these CSS variables instead of hardcoded colors.
Add .dark-theme class selector that overrides the CSS variables with dark theme values.
Ensure all UI elements including query syntax highlighting and result panels use these variables for color and background to maintain legibility in both themes.

implementation_steps.validation: CSS in styles.py includes both light and dark theme variables, existing styles use these variables, and .dark-theme class overrides variables correctly.

implementation_steps.description: Add a theme toggle button to the base HTML template and implement JavaScript to toggle themes and persist user preference in localStorage.

instructions: Locate the main HTML template rendering function or string that includes the <body> tag and header area.
Insert a button element with id='theme-toggle' and class='theme-toggle-btn' inside the header or navigation bar: <button id='theme-toggle' class='theme-toggle-btn'>🌙 Dark Mode</button>.
Add a <script> block just before the closing </body> tag containing JavaScript that:
- On page load, reads 'theme' from localStorage.
- Applies 'dark-theme' class to <body> if stored theme is 'dark'.
- Sets button text to '🌙 Dark Mode' if light theme active, or '☀️ Light Mode' if dark theme active.
- Adds a click event listener to the button to toggle the 'dark-theme' class on <body>, update localStorage with the new theme, and update the button text accordingly.
Add CSS styles for .theme-toggle-btn in the styles section or ensure it uses existing button styles for consistent UI.

implementation_steps.validation: HTML template includes the theme toggle button and embedded JavaScript that toggles theme, updates localStorage, and updates button text on user interaction.

implementation_steps.description: Create unit tests to verify theme toggle functionality and persistence behavior.

instructions: Write tests to simulate toggling the theme button and verify that the 'dark-theme' class is added or removed from the body element.
Test that the theme preference is saved to and read from localStorage correctly.
Test that the button text updates appropriately when toggling themes.
Use a headless browser testing framework or mock DOM environment to test JavaScript behavior if possible.
Include tests for initial page load applying the correct theme based on stored preference.

implementation_steps.validation: Unit tests cover theme toggle button functionality, localStorage persistence, and correct application of theme classes and button text.

implementation.pr_description: Implemented dark/light theme toggle feature with CSS variables for themes, a UI toggle button in the base HTML template, JavaScript to persist user preference in localStorage, and unit tests verifying theme toggle functionality and persistence.
